messages:
tim: Heads-up — hitting a reproducible long-context mem growth that looks like KV page table fragmentation + ghost pages on a mixed GPU fleet (H100 + RTX6000). Started after the kernel-selection tweak from last week.

nisha: Can you repro locally? steps?

tim: Yep. Repro with our longchat harness:
```
./tools/longchat_repro --model redwood/llama-70b-paged --context 65536 --seqs 1 --repeat 200 --backend paged_kvcache
```
It steadily climbs ~20MB per iteration on H100 (driver 535.x) until OOM. On RTX it plateaus.

evansnippet: Dump of page-table stats after ~120 iterations:
```
pt_total_entries: 131072
pt_allocated_pages: 10248
pt_free_runlists: 23
pt_fragmentation_ratio: 0.72
kvcache_reuse_window: 8
ghost_resident_pages: 409
```
(This is sanitized output from kvcache debug counters)

marta: "ghost_resident_pages" — do you mean pages that are accounted as resident but not referenced in any slotmap?

tim: Exactly. They appear in the PT but no owner slot. Suspect race between allocator free and pager eviction where we mark a page free but PT entry never cleared under certain kernel paths. Looks correlated with small-block kernel selection (the one that fragments allocations for kv-tiles).

infra-bot: CI test run scheduled: kvcache/pagetable-regressions (job #8421).

evansnippet: Quick stack trace from repro (stripped):
```
#0  kvcache_free_page
#1  kvcache_evict_cycle
#2  paged_attention_eviction_worker
#3  kernel_select_small_block
#4  schedule_workqueue
```

nisha: Interesting — only when kernel_select picks the small-block path? can you force the other path and confirm?

tim: Forced it by setting REDWOOD_KV_FORCE_KERNEL=large_block — growth disappears. So kernel selection + eviction ordering seems necessary.

evansnippet: Also saw this in NVLINK-mixed nodes where PCIe fallback triggers slightly different DMA ordering. Maybe a memory barrier missing when clearing PT bit.

marta: Repro matrix request: H100 driver 535.x, 520.x, A100 470.x, RTX6000 535.x. Also try with REDWOOD_KV_PT_DEBUG=1 to dump PT ops.

tim: Will run matrix tonight. For immediate mitigation: we can (1) force kernel selection to large_block in Dedicated pools, (2) add a sanity reclaim pass that walks PT and coalesces orphan pages every N iterations. Both are cheap rollouts.

evansnippet: Proposed patch idea (pseudo):
```
// after free, double-check owner under pt-lock
if (pt_entry->owner == NULL && pt_entry->res_cnt > 0) {
  // leak detected, clear and push page to free list
  pt_entry->res_cnt = 0;
  push_free(page);
}
```
Note: need to hold proper locks and avoid racing with eviction worker.

nisha: +1 to the temp mitigation. Also start a bisect for kernel-selection change (which commit diff?)

tim: Kernel select change came from 13f9b2a (perf: small-block allocator for tiled kv). Evan can you bisect?

evansnippet: On it. I'll bisect between 13f9b2a and previous and report by EOD. Also will attach the pmap + nvprof traces to the ticket.

marta: Filing an incident ticket in Jira: KVCACHE-498 (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/KVCACHE-498) with repro, logs, and proposed hotfix. Assign to eng-runtime.

infra-bot: Job kvcache/pagetable-regressions #8421 finished: flake detected on H100, attached logs to job.

tim: Thanks — once bisect narrows it down, let's plan a canary that forces large_block kernel selection + sanity reclaim on a small Dedicated pool. 

nisha: Also add unit to stress the 'free then immediate reassign' codepath. We probably missed that in CI.

tim: Agreed. I'll PR the sanity reclaim first and add the test.

evansnippet: Quick note: if anyone wants to reproduce locally, use this env to get verbose PT ops:
export REDWOOD_KV_PT_DEBUG=1; export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0; ./tools/longchat_repro ...

marta: Thanks — keep updates in KVCACHE-498. :thumbsup:
